query: Single-phase high-entropy alloys have difficulty achieving a satisfactory strength–ductility balance. Earlier work introduced the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with a uniform, fine lamellar structure to enable large-sized production and obtain good strength and plasticity, but its performance still falls short of industrial requirements. Its use in aircraft and spacecraft fasteners further requires stability under extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosion, while relevant creep and corrosion studies remain limited by sample-size and experimental-environment constraints. Given these limitations and design requirements, what single intervention could improve the alloy’s practical performance? Present one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, causal mechanism, predicted improvement over the starting material, boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a feasible experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a minor, controlled addition (0.2–0.5 wt%) of Y2O3 nanoparticles during melting and casting of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA, with advanced dispersion techniques, will pin grain and lamellar interfaces, thereby enhancing creep resistance, thermal stability, and corrosion resistance while maintaining a favorable strength–ductility balance.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with a fine lamellar structure exhibiting moderate strength and ductility but limited high-temperature stability, room-temperature creep resistance, and corrosion protection.
generation.intervention: Introduce 0.2–0.5 wt% Y2O3 nanoparticles via a reactive element addition during melting and casting, combined with vigorous stirring under an inert atmosphere to ensure uniform dispersion, followed by a short homogenization heat treatment (e.g., 1150°C for a brief period) to eliminate segregation.
generation.conditions: Casting under a controlled inert atmosphere with optimized stirring to achieve a fine and uniform dispersion of Y2O3 nanoparticles, followed by a homogenization heat treatment at elevated temperature (around 1150°C) and appropriate cooling to retain the lamellar microstructure.
generation.structural_mediator: Uniformly dispersed, stable oxide nanoparticles located at grain boundaries and lamellar interfaces that act as pinning centers.
generation.mechanism: The dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles impede grain boundary migration and dislocation motion, retarding microstructural coarsening during thermal cycling and reducing creep pathways. Additionally, they are expected to enhance corrosion resistance by promoting the formation of a stable and continuous passive oxide film on the material surface.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the baseline EHEA, the modified alloy will exhibit improved high-temperature stability and reduced room-temperature creep, as well as enhanced resistance to corrosive environments, while maintaining or moderately increasing the strength–ductility performance.
generation.baseline: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA with a uniform, fine lamellar structure and its associated mechanical and corrosion properties.
generation.boundary: The improvements will be realized only if uniform nanoparticle dispersion is achieved and maintained during service, i.e., the processing techniques must successfully prevent agglomeration and preserve the lamellar microstructure during high-temperature exposure and corrosion testing.
generation.uncertainty: The extent of improvement in long-term creep and corrosion resistance may vary with industrial-scale processing reproducibility of nanoparticle dispersion. The quantitative enhancement in performance is subject to variability depending on fine-tuning dispersion and homogenization conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA samples with varying Y2O3 additions (including control samples with no addition) using controlled casting with advanced stirring protocols. Subject these samples to standardized high-temperature thermal cycling, room-temperature creep tests under prolonged load, and accelerated corrosion tests (e.g., salt spray or molten salt environments). Compare the mechanical performance, creep rates, and corrosion resistance between modified and baseline samples.
measurements: Grain and particle dispersion analyses using EBSD and TEM
High-temperature thermal cycling tests with creep strain measurements
Room-temperature creep tests under defined mechanical loads
Corrosion rate assessment using electrochemical methods and salt spray exposure tests
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the samples with Y2O3 additions do not exhibit statistically significant improvements in high-temperature stability, reduced creep deformation, and enhanced corrosion resistance compared to the control samples, or if the modifications lead to a detrimental loss of ductility, then the hypothesis will be falsified.

cited_evidence.text: AbstractBoth crack-free AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) and Y and Hf co-doping AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA (YHf-EHEA) coatings were prepared by laser cladding. The solidification microstructure, thermal stability, and hot corrosion performance of the coatings at 900 °C under 75% Na2SO4 + 25% NaCl molten salts were investigated. The experimental results showed that the structure of the as-deposited coatings consisted of FCC and BCC/B2 phases. After heat treatment, an Al-rich L12 phase was precipitated in the FCC phase of all coatings. The grain sizes of the EHEA and YHf-EHEA coatings after heat treatment at 900 °C for 10 h increased by 27.5% and 15.7%, respectively, compared to the as-deposited coatings. Meanwhile, after hot corrosion, the spallation areas of the YHf-EHEA and EHEA coatings accounted for 14.98% and 5.67% of the total surface area, respectively. cited_evidence.text: In order to investigate the grain evolution of the coatings after heat treatment, EBSD analysis was performed on the coating surface. Figure 8a,d display the surface EBSD morphologies of the EHEA and YHf-EHEA coatings, respectively. It can be seen that the grains in the as-deposited coatings have a tendency to grow after heat treatment. From the statistical analysis of the average grain size and volume fraction of the low-angle grain boundaries (LAGBs) in both coatings after heat treatment, it can be observed that the grain sizes of the EHEA and YHf-EHEA coatings increased by 27.5% and 15.7%, respectively, compared to the as-deposited coatings. Additionally, the volume fractions of the LAGBs decreased by 13.9% and 8.3% in the EHEA and YHf-EHEA coatings, respectively. However, it can still be observed that the surface of the coating after heat treatment maintained a mixed structure of coarse and fine grains. proposals.intervention: Apply a dedicated post-casting aging heat treatment to induce in situ precipitation of coherent, nanoscale L12 intermetallic particles within the soft fcc lamellae.
proposals.conditions: Aging at ~600°C for several hours (time to be optimized) under an inert atmosphere to avoid unwanted oxidation.
proposals.structural_mediator: Formation of a fine dispersion of coherent L12 precipitates within the fcc phase.
proposals.mechanism: The L12 precipitates act as obstacles to dislocation motion, thereby increasing yield strength and creep resistance while also pinning lamellar interfaces to reduce coarsening during prolonged high-temperature exposure. The coherent precipitates can also modify local chemical ordering, which may improve passivation and corrosion behavior.
proposals.predicted_outcome: An enhanced strength–ductility balance with improved resistance to room-temperature creep and corrosion, compared to the untreated as-cast lamellar structure.
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This intervention targets the combined challenge of maintaining strength and ductility under extreme temperature fluctuations and long-term loading, while indirectly enhancing corrosion resistance. It is a single, process-level modification that builds on earlier evidence from precipitation strengthening in similar HEA systems.

proposals.intervention: Implement an advanced thermomechanical processing (TMP) regimen by combining severe plastic deformation (e.g., multi-pass cold rolling) with a subsequent controlled low-temperature annealing treatment.
proposals.conditions: Cold roll to a high reduction ratio (>70%) followed by annealing at ~500°C for a short duration (e.g., 30–60 minutes) in a protective atmosphere.
proposals.structural_mediator: Refinement of the lamellar spacing and enhancement of dislocation density at the fcc/B2 interfaces.
proposals.mechanism: Refined microstructure and increased interface area improve strain accommodation, impeding dislocation motion leading to increased strength and work hardening. The refined lamellae and strengthened interfaces also retard creep mechanisms and provide more uniform distribution of residual stresses, thus mitigating corrosion initiation sites.
proposals.predicted_outcome: A microstructure with a more uniform and finer lamellar architecture resulting in higher yield strength, improved ductility, reduced room-temperature creep, and enhanced resistance to thermal cycling-induced damage.
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: By modifying the microstructure via TMP, this intervention improves intrinsic mechanical properties and long-term stability under cyclic loads and temperature extremes, addressing the performance gaps of the baseline alloy.

proposals.intervention: Introduce a controlled oxide dispersion strengthening (ODS) strategy by adding a minor quantity (e.g., 0.2–0.5 wt%) of reactive Y2O3 nanoparticles into the melt during casting.
proposals.conditions: Casting under a controlled inert atmosphere with vigorous stirring to ensure uniform nanoparticle dispersion; followed by a homogenization heat treatment at elevated temperatures (e.g., 1150°C for a short duration) to eliminate segregation.
proposals.structural_mediator: Uniformly dispersed, stable oxide nanoparticles embedded at grain and lamellar interfaces.
proposals.mechanism: The oxide particles act as pinning centers for grain boundaries and inhibit dislocation motion. They additionally stabilize the microstructure against coarsening during thermal cycling and reduce pathways for creep deformation. As a bonus, the oxide particles contribute to the formation of a more robust passive film at the surface, enhancing corrosion resistance.
proposals.predicted_outcome: Improved high-temperature stability and creep resistance, along with enhanced corrosion performance, while maintaining or slightly increasing the strength–ductility balance relative to the baseline EHEA.
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This single intervention integrates dispersion strengthening to tackle both mechanical (creep, strength) and environmental (corrosion, thermal cycling) challenges required by fastener applications in aerospace and spacecraft.

proposals.intervention: Employ laser surface remelting (LSR) to generate a graded microstructure with a refined, passivated surface layer while preserving the bulk lamellar architecture.
proposals.conditions: Use a pulsed laser system with optimized scanning speed and energy density (parameters to be determined from preliminary trials) under an inert gas shield to remelt only the top ~50–100 μm of the alloy surface.
proposals.structural_mediator: A remodeled surface layer with ultrafine microstructure and enhanced local chemical order, possibly with a more continuous passive oxide film.
proposals.mechanism: The LSR process rapidly melts and re-solidifies the surface, resulting in grain refinement and suppression of segregation. The graded microstructure provides a hard, corrosion-resistant outer shell while maintaining ductility and toughness in the core. The improved passivation is expected to reduce localized corrosion and mitigate stress corrosion cracking under extreme conditions.
proposals.predicted_outcome: Enhanced surface hardness and corrosion resistance combined with improved fatigue behavior under mechanical loading, while retaining the beneficial bulk mechanical properties necessary for fastener applications.
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This targeted, single intervention addresses the need for environmental stability (corrosion, temperature fluctuations) and long-term mechanical loading effects without compromising the overall strength–ductility balance of the EHEA.

critiques.addresses_problem: Yes. The controlled oxide dispersion strategy directly aims to improve thermal stability, creep resistance, and corrosion performance—all issues that limit the current alloy's performance in extreme environments.
critiques.constraints: It is applied to the specified AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic alloy and is designed to enhance high-temperature and corrosion resistance while maintaining the strength–ductility balance; however, careful control of nanoparticle level is essential to avoid detrimentally affecting ductility.
critiques.physical_soundness: The mechanism is physically sound; oxide nanoparticles can serve as grain boundary pinning centers and impede dislocation motion, and can contribute to a better passive film formation.
critiques.feasibility: Yes, introducing oxides via controlled addition during casting combined with proper heat treatment is feasible with established ODS techniques.
critiques.evidence: The evidence in PMC10488378 shows that reactive element additions (Y, Hf) can improve thermal stability and corrosion resistance, which supports the idea, although the study used co-doping rather than pure Y2O3 additions.
critiques.main_risk: The main risk is the potential for nanoparticle agglomeration, which could create inhomogeneities or stress concentrators that might actually reduce ductility.
critiques.fix: Implement and optimize advanced stirring and dispersion techniques during casting to ensure uniform distribution of the Y2O3 particles.

critiques.addresses_problem: Yes. The post-casting aging treatment to induce coherent nanoscale L12 precipitates is designed to improve yield strength, creep resistance, and indirectly corrosion resistance, addressing the overall performance challenges.
critiques.constraints: It uses a heat treatment route constrained to the baseline AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy system while aiming to retain the promising lamellar structure and balancing strength with ductility.
critiques.physical_soundness: The mechanism is well-founded; precipitation strengthening via coherent L12 phases is an established approach in HEA systems and can impede dislocation motion effectively.
critiques.feasibility: Yes, controlled aging treatments are standard in metallurgy and have been applied in related eutectic HEA systems.
critiques.evidence: Studies cited in the provided records (e.g., PMC6478865 and related documents) support the effectiveness of inducing L12 precipitates in similar high-entropy alloy systems.
critiques.main_risk: The risk lies in potential over-aging or precipitate coarsening, which might lead to brittle intermetallic formation that compromises ductility.
critiques.fix: Carefully optimize aging temperature and time to control precipitate size and distribution, avoiding over-aging.

critiques.addresses_problem: Partially. Laser surface remelting addresses corrosion and fatigue issues by refining the surface microstructure and improving passivation, but it does not directly impact the bulk mechanical performance, creep resistance, or the overall strength–ductility balance required for fastener applications.
critiques.constraints: The intervention strictly modifies the surface layer without altering the bulk lamellar architecture; while this respects material and process constraints, it may not satisfy demands for high-temperature creep resistance and long-term mechanical loading across the whole component.
critiques.physical_soundness: The mechanism is sound for surface modification, improving hardness and corrosion resistance by refining the microstructure and promoting a continuous passive layer; however, its influence is limited to a shallow depth.
critiques.feasibility: Yes, laser surface remelting is an established technique with controllable parameters.
critiques.evidence: Although related studies (e.g., PMC10488378 and PMC6353877) discuss surface modifications and corrosion protection in HEAs, there is no direct evidence that LSR sufficiently improves bulk properties such as creep resistance.
critiques.main_risk: The main risk is that the intervention improves only the surface properties while leaving the bulk unaltered, which may not sufficiently enhance overall performance under long-term mechanical loading and thermal cycling.
critiques.fix: Increase the remelted layer thickness or depth to affect a larger volume fraction of the material, thereby exerting a more significant influence on bulk performance.

critiques.addresses_problem: Yes. Advanced thermomechanical processing (TMP) targets improvement of the internal microstructure by refining the lamellar spacing and enhancing interface strength, leading to a better balance of strength and ductility, as well as potential improvements in creep resistance and corrosion performance.
critiques.constraints: It maintains the material system and is applied post-casting, utilizing severe plastic deformation and controlled annealing without introducing foreign phases, aligning with the specified operational constraints.
critiques.physical_soundness: The mechanism is physically plausible; refining the microstructure via plastic deformation and controlled annealing is known to improve yield strength and work hardening, although care must be taken to preserve ductility.
critiques.feasibility: Yes, severe plastic deformation techniques and subsequent annealing are well-established in the processing of high-entropy alloys.
critiques.evidence: Evidence from studies (e.g., PMC5818523 and PMC6353877) supports that TMP can refine microstructures and improve mechanical properties in HEAs, although sometimes at the risk of embrittlement.
critiques.main_risk: The main risk is that excessive plastic deformation might lead to embrittlement or non-uniform microstructures that adversely affect ductility and reliability under cyclic loading.
critiques.fix: Optimize the reduction ratio and annealing parameters to achieve uniform microstructural refinement without inducing embrittlement.

decision.rationale: Direction A directly targets the material's deficits by introducing a controlled oxide dispersion strengthening strategy. The use of a small addition of Y2O3 nanoparticles is designed to pin grain and lamellar boundaries, inhibit dislocation motion, and improve microstructural stability during thermal cycling. This intervention also promotes a more robust passive film formation at the surface, addressing both creep and corrosion issues, which are critical for aerospace fastener applications. Although there is a risk of nanoparticle agglomeration that could reduce ductility, the suggested fix of implementing advanced stirring/dispersion techniques during casting is a viable mitigation strategy, according to supporting evidence from PMC10488378.
